sections.kicker: Prepared for blond & braun by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: blond & braun already has a colour and an idea. The page leads with a title.
sections.keep: The deep plum on the banner, the book and the button. It is the one colour that makes the brand recognisable.

pins.quote: Knjiga za parove koja potiče jednostavne i duboke razgovore kroz ljudsko osmišljena pitanja
pins.what: The description holds a real difference: the questions are written by people.
pins.why: On a shelf of conversation card decks, human-written questions are the reason to pick this one, and the idea sits in the middle of a sentence.
pins.how: Pull the human-made idea out and make it the headline.
pins.label: Your description
pins.cost: The book reads as one more question deck.

pins.what: The book title is the loudest thing on the page, bigger than the brand name.
pins.why: Two names compete at the top, the product and blond & braun, and a buyer remembers only one.
pins.how: Decide which name people should repeat, then make it the larger one.
pins.label: Your title
pins.cost: Word of mouth carries a book title and not the brand.

pins.area: Living room photographed through a reflective window under the hero
pins.what: The photo under the hero is shot through a window, with reflections across the room.
pins.why: The plum book image is composed, and the next one looks like a phone snapshot, so the look changes in one scroll.
pins.how: Use one photographic style from the first image to the last.
pins.label: Your photography
pins.cost: The brand looks designed in one place and casual in the next.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at blond & braun. I spent some time on your site. Three things stood out, and they point the same way.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on blond & braun's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
sections.note: A few short questions first, then you pick a time. You can also just reply to the email.

reference: Penguin Books, from another category. Its orange spines made a publisher recognisable before anyone read a title.
